key_insight: Ceramic performance is controlled by the processing–microstructure–property chain, where atomic bonding, defects, grain size, porosity, and phase stability jointly determine mechanical, thermal, electrical, and biological behavior.
engineering_relevance: The review highlights how processing choices such as sintering, sol–gel, and additive manufacturing can be used to tailor densification, geometry, composition, and biomedical functionality in advanced ceramic components.
method: Conventional sintering to control densification and grain growth
Sol–gel processing for composition and microstructure control
Additive manufacturing for complex geometry and multimaterial fabrication
evidence_signal: This is a review article synthesizing reported relationships across ceramics, rather than presenting new experimental data or a single quantitative evaluation.
watch_item: A major implementation concern is the porosity–strength trade-off, since defects, heterogeneity, and residual stresses can strongly reduce fracture resistance.
paper_title: Ceramic Materials: From Atomic Bonding and Processing to Microstructure, Functional Properties, and Biomedical Applications
